claims.text: The thesis exhibits excellent citation hygiene, drawing correctly on foundational works by Murray, Brylinski, and Wockel. Key modern developments by Waldorf and Ganter are well-integrated into the construction of the categorical Hopf map. The bibliography is comprehensive and accurately reflects the intersection of higher category theory and differential geometry required for this research.
This is a foundational reference for the formalism of principal 2-bundles (categorical principal bundles) used extensively throughout the paper to construct the categorical Hopf map.
Defines the categorical circle U(1), which serves as the fiber for the categorical Hopf map introduced in the paper.
The original paper introducing the Hopf map, which the author categorifies.
Introduces bundle gerbes, which are essential for the paper's discussion on higher categorical structures and the factorization of the categorical Hopf map.
Introduces the String group, which is central to the author's final conjecture regarding symmetries of the categorical Hopf map.
Provides a finite-dimensional categorical model for the String group, used in the classification of the categorical Hopf map's fiber and for cohomology calculations.
Used as a comparative framework for Waldorf's approach to gerbes and principal 2-bundles versus Wockel's.
A key reference for the connection formalism on principal 2-bundles, specifically used in the context of the categorical Hopf map's connection.
Used for background on central extensions and loop groups, specifically in relating these to the String group symmetries.

The Hopf map is a celebrated construction in topology that shows how to map a 3-sphere continuously to a 2-sphere in a non-trivial way, forming a principal bundle with circle symmetry. This thesis extends this classical object into categorical geometry—a higher-dimensional algebraic setting where geometric structures are enriched with categorical data.
